claims.text: The grant will support BES members to deliver independent outreach, public engagement, and science communication activities.
These activities should engage public audiences with the excitement, importance, and relevance of ecological science.
Alternatively, the activities can enhance the experience and skills of others to communicate ecology with public audiences.
The grant will support diverse formats, including in-person events, digital formats, or physical resources.
Projects should aim to communicate evidence-based messaging about ecology, how nature works, and the use of ecological science as a solution to challenges.
Projects should raise awareness and public understanding of ecological careers, their relevance, importance, breadth, and diversity.
Projects should show how individuals can take action to benefit the environment, themselves, and society.
Projects should increase the ability of others to deliver the above aims through outreach and engagement activities.
The grant encourages applications for activities that pilot novel methods of communicating ecological sciences with public audiences.
The grant encourages engagement that may stimulate dialogue with ecologists, inform behavioral change and action, or encourage ecological career prospects.
The grant encourages interdisciplinary collaborations.
The grant encourages the production of engagement materials or outcomes that others can use or benefit from subsequently.
The grant encourages the development of skills in communicating ecological science with public audiences, such as through training.
The lead applicant must have a BES membership.
Projects should be a maximum of 12 months in duration.
Awards are open to individuals, teams, and organizations across all experience levels.
Collaborations between two or more people are welcome.
Proposals must be aimed at a non-academic audience.
All projects must clearly demonstrate direct interaction with a non-academic audience.
Projects should show evidence of links to the research community at regional, national, and international levels, where appropriate.
There are no restrictions on where applicants come from.
There are no restrictions on where applicants carry out their outreach and engagement work.
Applications will not be considered for staff salaries, except for one-off costs relevant to completing the event like sub-contracting for logo design.
Training courses not associated with developing skills in communicating the science of ecology for a public-facing audience are not eligible.
Projects aimed solely at delivering curriculum to school children are not eligible.
Projects delivered to a small number (1-2) of schools in a school setting where other members of the public cannot engage are not eligible.
Applications from museums and schools are welcome, but projects must involve significant outreach beyond schools.
No more than one grant will be awarded to any applicant in any year.
No more than three grants will be awarded to any applicant in any five years.
Failure to submit a satisfactory report at the end of a grant will make the applicant ineligible for further grants.
Repeat, annual events will only be considered if the project shows new novel ideas and development on the previous application.
The maximum award is £2,000.
The award may be used as part-funding for larger projects involving other sponsors.
If the BES grant is used to part-fund a project, there must be a guarantee that other funding has already been secured.
If other funding has been secured, the additional BES funding should add a distinctive element/activity that would not happen otherwise and will greatly enhance outreach activities.
